title: Sell Mineral Rights in Jerusalem, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Jerusalem, OH
metaDescription: Jerusalem sits in Monroe County, in Ohio's Utica/Point Pleasant core. Learn what active development in this area means for your mineral interest.
heroLead: Jerusalem sits in Monroe County farm country, where drilling has reached deep into land that stayed in the same families for generations before Utica ever came up.
intro: Jerusalem is a small unincorporated community in Monroe County, one of the more consistently active counties in the Utica/Point Pleasant core since the play's early years. Land around Jerusalem was farmed for generations before drilling arrived, with minerals frequently severed through simple family deeds, and today many of those tracts sit within active spacing units drilled by operators working the broader Monroe County fairway.

sections.heading: Monroe County's consistent core activity
paragraphs: Monroe County has hosted steady horizontal development for over a decade, with real production history built up across many of its townships, including the area around Jerusalem. That track record means a mineral owner here can often find comparable well data even if their specific tract hasn't been drilled directly, which helps ground any valuation conversation in real numbers rather than guesswork.

sections.heading: Farm-family severances and confirming your share
paragraphs: Most mineral reservations around Jerusalem trace back to farm deeds written in simple fractional language, and after multiple generations of inheritance, it's common for the current ownership to be split among several descendants. A title search through the Monroe County Recorder's office in Woodsfield will confirm your exact current decimal interest and whether it's tied to a producing unit.

faqs.question: Is Jerusalem in an actively producing part of Monroe County?
faqs.answer: Monroe County has seen consistent Utica development, and many tracts near Jerusalem sit within that activity, though results vary parcel to parcel.

faqs.question: How do I confirm my exact share if the interest passed through multiple generations?
faqs.answer: A title search tracing the original severance deed through every subsequent inheritance will confirm your current fractional interest relative to other heirs.

faqs.question: What documents should I gather before contacting a buyer?
faqs.answer: Your deed, any lease or division order, and recent royalty statements if you have them, which together establish your net mineral acres and decimal interest.

faqs.question: Could my family's minerals be at risk under the Dormant Mineral Act?
faqs.answer: If the interest has never been leased or produced and never appeared in a recorded title transaction for 20 straight years, it could be vulnerable to an abandonment claim, so it's worth checking the recorder's index periodically.

faqs.question: Do I need an attorney to sell my Monroe County mineral interest?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily for the sale itself, but if your chain of title includes unclear heirship or a DMA notice, legal guidance can prevent complications before closing.
